data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Independent operation is neither necessary nor sufficient for true resilience, because a shared monoculture (same OS, library, or CDN) causes failures to be perfectly correlated exactly when that hidden common cause fails, regardless of the operator topology, while a single large service can achieve true independence by formally isolating its redundant subsystems.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Evidence that the small services deliberately use non-overlapping dependency stacks (e.g., one on Linux/nginx, another on Windows/IIS) with verified absence of shared third-party libraries would break the monoculture hazard, restoring independence to the decentralized case.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Evidence that a single large service is constrained by economics to use the exact same dependency stack for every redundant instance, and therefore cannot achieve formal isolation, would negate the large-service independence argument.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A formal proof that formal isolation is impossible at acceptable cost for a single large service would weaken the claim.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A monocultured fleet of small services shares a hidden common cause (e.g., all nodes use the same TLS library), so failures appear independent during normal operation but become perfectly correlated at the threshold of a bug in the shared cause, which necessarily annihilates the independence advantage, whereas a single large service can encode true independence by enforcing formally verified isolation domains (different OS kernels, compiler toolchains, and power grids) across its redundant instances, making the correlated-failure hazard a direct function of shared-dependency surface rather than operator count.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
